observations.description: what you read in the ledger and the tool results

rethink.description: earlier whys looked at again in the light of results that came in after them: does each still hold?

id.description: the earlier why's own id, for example Y1 (never a K number: those are the numbers of rethinks)

in_light_of.description: the results you look at it again with: ids of evidence tables, checks or verdicts that came in after it (for example E2, C3)

now.description: what it is now: verify (still open and worth verifying), set_aside (not now), refuted (the results speak against it), supported (the results speak for it: its hypotheses held)

because.description: what in those results makes it so, in one sentence

about.description: the records whose result this is about: ids of evidence tables, simulations, checks or verdicts in the ledger (for example E2, C3), or the word brief

result.description: the result, in one sentence: what came out, and what is surprising or unexplained in it

guess.description: your informed guess of why it came out so

unseen.description: what in the system, not directly visible in the measures, would make it so

matters.description: how it could matter for the goal if the guess is true

worth.description: verify: worth verifying now for the goal; set_aside: not now

reason.description: why it is, or is not, worth verifying now

anyOf.description: the id of an earlier why that this one replaces with a better guess (for example Y1)

whys.description: informed guesses of why results came out as they did; from those worth verifying come the hypotheses

from_why.description: the id of the why this hypothesis comes from (one you chose to verify), for example Y2

question.description: the hypothesis put as one plain question of at most 20 words, for a reader who is not a specialist

why.description: why answering this question helps reach the goal: one plain sentence of at most 25 words

prediction.description: falsifiable: a number, a range or a direction

follows_from.description: may be left empty: the harness takes it from the why's about

drop.description: open hypotheses you give up without a verdict; may be empty

tests.description: test: ids of the open hypotheses it tests; explore: empty

question.description: explore: what you want to find out; test: may be empty

for.description: the id of the tested hypothesis this is for

to_know.description: one plain sentence: what you must know to decide this hypothesis

varies.description: the one knob whose value differs between the simulations made for it; none when a single simulation against a stated number decides it

simulations.description: the labels of the simulations made for this hypothesis, and of no other design

needs.description: test: one entry for each tested hypothesis, written before the simulations: what must be known to decide it, and the simulations made for that; explore: empty

measurements.description: measurements of your own that this experiment takes of each of its simulations, beside the outputs; empty when you need none. A decision rule and a need may name them like an output

name.description: a name of its own: lower-case letters, digits and _, for example rwnd_mean

of.description: a column a simulation records over time, or arithmetic over columns of one record, for example rwnd or inflight / rwnd

t_from.description: the window's start in seconds of the simulation; null: the start of the measured seconds (2)

t_to.description: the window's end; null: the end of the simulation

level.description: the number time_above and the like compare with; null for the other statistics

with.description: for corr and lag only: the second column, or arithmetic over columns of the same record, that of is compared with; null otherwise

items.description: a knob of the brief (loop.py lists the brief's knobs here at the start of a session)

varied.description: the knobs that differ between the simulations

anyOf.description: label of the simulation the others are compared with

params.description: a value for every knob of the brief. loop.py puts the object in place of this one at the start of a session, built from the session's brief: one property per knob, in the brief's order, all required

decision_rules.description: test: at least one decision rule per tested hypothesis, stated before the simulations; explore: empty

decision_rule.description: a comparison the harness will check, e.g. measure@label > 1.1 * measure@otherlabel

rival.description: a competing explanation of how the system behaves

rival_predicts.description: what this decision rule would give if the rival were true

verdicts.description: only for hypotheses that have a checked decision rule; may be empty

goal.description: the goal used; for an open brief: the goal you chose, and why

recommendation.description: the settings you recommend: knobs only, each within its range

expected.description: the output values you expect at the recommendation

no_difference.description: the knobs whose tested values made no meaningful difference to the goal (differences inside the tolerance); empty only if every knob you varied mattered; never a knob you did not vary

limit.description: what limits the result at the recommendation, that is, why it is not better: the cause and the ledger ids that show it; if you did not find it, say so and what you would test next

explanation.description: why this setting is best, building on limit and no_difference

holds_when.description: conditions under which the answer stays valid

breaks_when.description: conditions under which it would change

role.description: what the claim does in your answer: supports (a reason for the recommendation), background (how the system behaves), limits (when the recommendation would change)

items.description: a ledger id, e.g. E3 or C5

simulations.description: how many more simulations to add to the budget

why.description: one sentence: why they are needed
